b-rubrik-cohesity-backup-dell-powerprote.title: Enterprise backup management API exposed
b-rubrik-cohesity-backup-dell-powerprote.why: A reachable Rubrik, Cohesity, or Dell PowerProtect API identifies a high-value management plane that commonly holds infrastructure inventories and privileged integration credentials. Attackers target backup systems to steal data and impair recovery before disruptive operations.

fix.label: Restrict management access
fix.text: Place the backup API on a dedicated management network and permit access only from approved administration hosts and monitoring systems.

fix.label: Harden administrator authentication
fix.text: Require MFA or centralized identity for administrators, remove dormant accounts, rotate integration credentials, and install supported security updates.

bartifact-docker-registry-sonatype-nexus.title: Artifact repository or registry exposed
bartifact-docker-registry-sonatype-nexus.why: An exposed Docker Registry, Nexus, Artifactory, or Harbor service reveals a software-supply-chain management plane and may disclose repository names, versions, or internal package metadata. Compromise of a privileged account could let an attacker obtain proprietary artifacts or tamper with software consumed by deployment pipelines.

fix.label: Limit registry reachability
fix.text: Expose the service only to authorized developer, CI, and administration networks through firewall rules or an authenticated reverse proxy.

fix.label: Enforce repository controls
fix.text: Disable anonymous access unless explicitly required, apply least-privilege repository roles, require MFA for administrators, and use separate scoped CI tokens.

bartifact-docker-registry-unauth-catalog.title: Docker Registry catalog allows anonymous access
bartifact-docker-registry-unauth-catalog.why: The registry catalog can be listed without authentication, exposing repository names and potentially enabling anonymous tag or manifest enumeration. These details reveal internal applications and versions that help attackers identify sensitive images and vulnerable components.

fix.label: Require registry authentication
fix.text: Configure the registry or its reverse proxy to require authentication for catalog, repository, tag, manifest, pull, and push operations.

fix.label: Restrict network access
fix.text: Limit registry access to approved CI workers, deployment systems, and administrator networks.

bauth-ok-b-18ccdbe4.title: RabbitMQ management credentials accepted
bauth-ok-b-18ccdbe4.why: Operator-supplied credentials successfully authenticated to the RabbitMQ management API. Depending on their assigned tags and virtual-host permissions, the account may expose users, queues, exchanges, messages, connections, or administrative functions.

fix.label: Review the authenticated account
fix.text: Confirm that the account is expected, rotate it if its use is unexplained, and restrict its RabbitMQ tags and virtual-host permissions to the minimum required.

fix.label: Protect the management API
fix.text: Restrict management API access to administration networks, require TLS, and use centralized authentication or MFA where supported.

bbmc-hpe-ilo-dell-idrac-supermicro-ipmi-.title: Server baseboard management controller exposed
bbmc-hpe-ilo-dell-idrac-supermicro-ipmi-.why: A reachable iLO, iDRAC, IPMI, XCC, IMM, or CIMC interface provides out-of-band control that can remain available even when the operating system is offline. Administrative compromise may permit console access, power control, virtual-media mounting, firmware changes, or recovery bypass.

fix.label: Isolate out-of-band management
fix.text: Move BMC interfaces to a dedicated management network with firewall or jump-host enforcement and no direct Internet or user-LAN access.

fix.label: Harden controller access
fix.text: Change default credentials, disable unused legacy protocols, require MFA where supported, install current firmware, and forward audit events to monitoring.

bcommvault-detected-5f2f4842.title: Commvault management service exposed
bcommvault-detected-5f2f4842.why: A reachable Commvault web service exposes a backup-management plane with visibility into protected systems, stored data, and operational credentials. Attackers frequently target backup infrastructure to obtain broad access and prevent reliable restoration.

fix.label: Restrict CommServe access
fix.text: Allow the web service only from dedicated administration and backup networks, preferably through a controlled jump host.

fix.label: Harden and update Commvault
fix.text: Apply supported maintenance releases, require strong administrator authentication, rotate service credentials, and review roles and audit logs.

bdefault-cred-6077e4eb.title: Default credentials accepted
bdefault-cred-6077e4eb.why: A service accepted a vendor-default or commonly shipped credential pair. Attackers routinely test these credentials because they can provide immediate administrative access without exploiting a software vulnerability.

fix.label: Replace the default credential
fix.text: Set a unique, randomly generated password or managed service credential and invalidate every vendor-default account or secret.

fix.label: Check for prior use
fix.text: Review authentication and configuration logs for access using the default credential, rotate related secrets, and investigate unexplained activity.

bdell-avamar-powerprotect-legacy-service.title: Legacy Avamar or PowerProtect service reachable
bdell-avamar-powerprotect-legacy-service.why: A legacy Dell Avamar or PowerProtect service is reachable over the network, increasing the attack surface of a system that stores or controls backups. Older management protocols may lack modern authentication and transport protections and should not be accessible from general-purpose networks.

test.label: Confirm and fingerprint the TCP service

fix.label: Restrict the legacy service
fix.text: Allow the port only between documented backup components on a dedicated network and block it from user, guest, and Internet-facing segments.

fix.label: Upgrade or retire the interface
fix.text: Install current supported PowerProtect or Avamar releases and disable legacy listeners that are no longer required.

bhypervisor-vmware-esxi-host-proxmox-ve-.title: Hypervisor management plane exposed
bhypervisor-vmware-esxi-host-proxmox-ve-.why: A VMware ESXi, Proxmox VE, or Nutanix Prism management interface is reachable. These systems control many workloads, so stolen administrator access or exploitation can expose virtual disks, consoles, snapshots, credentials, and multiple hosted services at once.

fix.label: Segment hypervisor management
fix.text: Permit access only from a dedicated management network and approved jump hosts; block direct access from user networks and the Internet.

fix.label: Harden privileged access
fix.text: Require MFA or centralized identity, remove unused local administrators, apply security updates, and alert on privileged logins and configuration changes.

bkey-only-b-adfd43e9.title: SSH permits public-key authentication only
bkey-only-b-adfd43e9.why: The SSH server advertises public-key authentication but not password or keyboard-interactive authentication. This reduces password-spraying risk, but defenders must still protect private keys, constrain authorized keys, and remove stale access because possession of a trusted key may be sufficient for login.

test.label: Read advertised SSH authentication methods
test.cmd: ssh -vv -p <port> -o BatchMode=yes -o PreferredAuthentications=none -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null <user>@<host> true 2>&1 | grep -i 'authentication methods'

fix.label: Maintain key-only authentication
fix.text: Keep password authentication disabled, inventory authorized keys, remove stale keys, and require passphrases or hardware-backed keys for privileged access.

fix.label: Constrain key privileges
fix.text: Apply least privilege to SSH accounts and use authorized_keys restrictions such as source-address, command, or forwarding constraints where appropriate.

bopenstack-keystone-detected-856681df.title: OpenStack Keystone API exposed
bopenstack-keystone-detected-856681df.why: A reachable Keystone endpoint identifies the identity control plane for an OpenStack environment and can disclose API versions and service topology. Although version discovery may be intentionally public, unnecessary reachability increases reconnaissance value and exposes a high-impact authentication surface.

fix.label: Restrict identity API exposure
fix.text: Expose administrative Keystone endpoints only to trusted management networks and publish only the interfaces required by legitimate clients.

fix.label: Harden Keystone
fix.text: Use TLS, federated or MFA-protected administrative identities, least-privilege roles, supported releases, and centralized audit logging.

bplatform-hashicorp-nomad-portainer-ranc.title: Workload platform control plane exposed
bplatform-hashicorp-nomad-portainer-ranc.why: A Nomad, Portainer, Rancher, or Argo CD control plane is reachable and reveals a high-value workload-management surface. Compromised access could expose cluster inventories, deployment configuration, registry credentials, secrets, or the ability to alter running applications.

test.label: Probe product discovery endpoints
test.cmd: for p in /v1/status/leader /api/status /v3/settings/server-version /api/version; do curl -k -i '<service>://<host>:<port>'"$p"; done

fix.label: Restrict control-plane access
fix.text: Limit the interface to trusted administration and cluster networks through firewall rules, a VPN, or an authenticated access proxy.

fix.label: Enforce strong authorization
fix.text: Enable the product's authentication and authorization features, require SSO and MFA for administrators, use scoped automation tokens, and remove anonymous access.

bplatform-nomad-unauth-job-inventory-f09.title: Nomad job inventory accessible anonymously
bplatform-nomad-unauth-job-inventory-f09.why: The Nomad jobs API returns workload inventory without authentication. Job names, namespaces, types, and deployment metadata reveal internal architecture and can guide attacks against applications, images, or supporting services.

fix.label: Enable Nomad ACLs
fix.text: Enable the Nomad ACL system, set an appropriate default-deny policy, and grant job-listing permissions only to authenticated identities that require them.

fix.label: Limit API reachability
fix.text: Bind or firewall the HTTP API so it is reachable only from trusted cluster and administration networks, and require TLS for remote clients.

bpotential-cred-leak-b-314c9b48.title: Potential credentials exposed through search data
bpotential-cred-leak-b-314c9b48.why: A read-only Elasticsearch query found documents matching credential-related terms such as passwords, secrets, or tokens. Search indexes often aggregate logs and application records, so anonymous or overprivileged query access can expose reusable credentials at scale.

fix.label: Require authenticated search access
fix.text: Enable Elasticsearch security, block anonymous cluster access, and grant index privileges only to applications and users with a documented need.

fix.label: Remove and rotate exposed secrets
fix.text: Identify the originating data source, purge unnecessary secret-bearing records according to retention policy, and rotate every credential that may have been indexed.

brmi-registry-02db4e39.title: Java RMI registry exposed
brmi-registry-02db4e39.why: A reachable Java RMI registry can disclose bound object names, remote endpoints, and implementation details. Exposed registries also increase the risk from unsafe remote-object configurations or vulnerable applications registered behind them.

fix.label: Restrict registry reachability
fix.text: Bind the registry to an internal interface where possible and firewall it so only explicitly authorized application hosts can connect.

fix.label: Harden registered services
fix.text: Remove obsolete bindings, avoid exposing unsafe remote methods or serialized-object entry points, and update the JRE and hosting application.

bslp-open-service-registry-b7a3b96f.title: Service Location Protocol registry exposed
bslp-open-service-registry-b7a3b96f.why: A reachable SLP service registry permits network clients to discover advertised services and related attributes. Internet or broad-network exposure assists reconnaissance and may also expose implementations affected by historical SLP vulnerabilities or amplification abuse.

test.label: Check for a TCP SLP listener

fix.label: Disable SLP when unnecessary
fix.text: Disable the SLP daemon or product integration if service discovery is not required.

fix.label: Constrain SLP traffic
fix.text: Permit SLP only within the smallest required management segment and block TCP and UDP port 427 at external and inter-segment boundaries.

bsource-ci-gerrit-atlassian-confluence-a.title: Source or Atlassian service exposed
bsource-ci-gerrit-atlassian-confluence-a.why: A Gerrit, Confluence, Jira, or Bamboo interface is reachable and may reveal project names, users, versions, build information, or internal documentation. These systems frequently contain source-code context and integration credentials, making their administrative and anonymous-access boundaries important attack paths.

test.label: Probe product information endpoints
test.cmd: for p in /config/server/version /status /rest/api/2/serverInfo /rest/api/latest/info; do curl -k -i '<service>://<host>:<port>'"$p"; done

fix.label: Restrict anonymous visibility
fix.text: Disable unneeded anonymous project, issue, page, build, and user-directory access and review all public or broadly shared content.

fix.label: Protect administration
fix.text: Require SSO and MFA for administrators, apply current vendor security updates, scope integration tokens, and restrict management interfaces to trusted networks.

bsource-ci-teamcity-github-enterprise-az.title: Enterprise source or CI service exposed
bsource-ci-teamcity-github-enterprise-az.why: A TeamCity, GitHub Enterprise, or Azure DevOps Server interface is reachable and may expose organization, repository, build, or version metadata. These platforms hold source code and powerful automation credentials, so compromised access can affect both intellectual property and the software supply chain.

test.label: Probe service metadata endpoints
test.cmd: for p in /app/rest/server /api/v3/meta '/_apis/connectionData?connectOptions=0'; do curl -k -i '<service>://<host>:<port>'"$p"; done

fix.label: Limit external reachability
fix.text: Publish only required user-facing endpoints and restrict administrative, agent, and maintenance interfaces to trusted networks.

fix.label: Harden identities and tokens
fix.text: Require SSO and MFA, disable anonymous access, use short-lived least-privilege automation tokens, protect build agents, and apply vendor security updates promptly.

bthickclient-rdp-creds-vpn-profile-brows.title: Local client credential artifact present
bthickclient-rdp-creds-vpn-profile-brows.why: An RDP credential reference, VPN profile, or browser login database exists on the assessed workstation. Even when values are encrypted, an attacker with local user access may recover connection targets, usernames, tokens, or secrets using the user's security context.

fix.label: Remove unnecessary saved access
fix.text: Delete obsolete profiles and cached credentials through the owning application, and configure clients to avoid retaining credentials where operationally practical.

fix.label: Protect workstation secrets
fix.text: Use full-disk encryption, strong screen-lock policy, endpoint protection, and separate privileged accounts; require MFA for RDP and VPN services.

bthickclient-sshkey-at-rest-saved-sessio.title: High-risk client secret stored locally
bthickclient-sshkey-at-rest-saved-sessio.why: A private SSH key, saved session, credential store, or configuration secret was found on the workstation. Local compromise could turn these artifacts into immediate access to servers, databases, file-transfer systems, or administrative interfaces.

fix.label: Move secrets into managed storage
fix.text: Replace plaintext or reversibly stored credentials with an approved password manager, operating-system credential vault, hardware-backed key, or short-lived identity mechanism.

fix.label: Rotate affected credentials
fix.text: Rotate any key, password, or token whose local protection or access history cannot be assured, then remove stale saved sessions and secret-bearing configuration files.

bunauth-proxmox-version-api-exposed-8638.title: Proxmox version API accessible anonymously
bunauth-proxmox-version-api-exposed-8638.why: The Proxmox API returns release, version, and repository information without authentication. This gives attackers a reliable product fingerprint for vulnerability matching and confirms the location of a high-impact virtualization management plane.

fix.label: Restrict the Proxmox API
fix.text: Limit management-interface access to a dedicated administration network, VPN, or authenticated proxy even if the version endpoint itself cannot be disabled.

fix.label: Maintain current packages
fix.text: Apply supported Proxmox VE and Debian security updates and monitor the management plane for unexpected reconnaissance and login activity.

buser-exists-b-90f92a5a.title: XMPP account existence can be inferred
buser-exists-b-90f92a5a.why: The XMPP authentication flow produced a response or repeatable timing difference that may distinguish an existing username. Reliable account enumeration helps attackers construct targeted password-spraying and social-engineering campaigns, although results should be compared with randomized controls to exclude uniform SASL failures.

test.label: Repeat SASL differential checks with controls

fix.label: Normalize authentication failures
fix.text: Configure or update the XMPP server and identity backend so nonexistent and valid accounts receive indistinguishable SASL failure responses and comparable processing times.

fix.label: Limit automated probing
fix.text: Rate-limit failed authentication attempts, monitor distributed enumeration patterns, require MFA where supported, and avoid exposing unnecessary user-directory information.

bvault-not-initialized-claim-init-opport.title: HashiCorp Vault is not initialized
bvault-not-initialized-claim-init-opport.why: The Vault API reports that the instance has not been initialized. The first party to initialize it receives the initial root token and key shares, so an attacker who reaches this state could claim control of the new Vault before its owner completes provisioning.

fix.label: Restrict access immediately
fix.text: Block untrusted network access to the Vault API before initialization; do not allow testing personnel or unattended automation to initialize the instance.

fix.label: Perform a controlled initialization ceremony
fix.text: Have designated custodians initialize Vault using the approved seal design, securely distribute recovery material, protect the initial root token, and revoke it after setup.

bveeam-b-r-rest-detected-dbcaa69e.title: Veeam Backup REST API exposed
bveeam-b-r-rest-detected-dbcaa69e.why: A reachable Veeam Backup & Replication REST endpoint identifies a high-value backup-management system and may disclose version or authentication details. Veeam servers commonly possess broad infrastructure access, and vulnerable or stolen administrative access can undermine both protected workloads and recovery data.

fix.label: Restrict the REST API
fix.text: Allow API access only from designated backup administration hosts and automation systems on a protected management network.

fix.label: Patch and protect Veeam
fix.text: Install current Veeam security updates, require strong unique administrative identities, rotate service credentials, and monitor privileged API activity.

bveritas-netbackup-detected-8aa2feba.title: Veritas NetBackup service exposed
bveritas-netbackup-detected-8aa2feba.why: A reachable NetBackup service reveals backup infrastructure that may communicate with many protected hosts and storage systems. Compromise can expose backup data, privileged service relationships, and the organization's ability to recover from destructive activity.

fix.label: Restrict NetBackup communications
fix.text: Permit the service only between documented NetBackup components and administration hosts on protected backup networks.

fix.label: Update and audit NetBackup
fix.text: Apply supported security fixes, remove obsolete clients and trust relationships, rotate service credentials, and review administrator and restore activity.

bvmware-vcenter-sdk-reachable-24c791fc.title: VMware vCenter SDK endpoint exposed
bvmware-vcenter-sdk-reachable-24c791fc.why: The vCenter SDK endpoint is reachable and exposes the automation interface for managing virtual infrastructure. While authentication is normally required, unnecessary reachability provides a precise management-plane target and increases the impact of stolen credentials or unpatched vulnerabilities.

fix.label: Restrict SDK access
fix.text: Allow the SDK only from approved management and automation hosts, and block it from Internet-facing and user workstation networks.

fix.label: Harden API identities
fix.text: Use dedicated least-privilege service accounts, rotate automation credentials, require MFA for human administrators, and keep vCenter fully patched.

bvmware-vcenter-ui-a99e5695.title: VMware vCenter management UI exposed
bvmware-vcenter-ui-a99e5695.why: A reachable vCenter web interface identifies the central management plane for VMware infrastructure. Compromised administrative access can affect numerous virtual machines, networks, datastores, snapshots, and console sessions.

fix.label: Segment vCenter management
fix.text: Restrict the UI to a dedicated management network, approved jump hosts, or a strongly authenticated administrative access proxy.

fix.label: Protect administrator access
fix.text: Require MFA through the configured identity provider, remove stale privileged accounts, apply vCenter updates, and alert on unusual login or role changes.

defaultpassword-4522eb4c.title: Windows AutoLogon password stored in registry
defaultpassword-4522eb4c.why: The Winlogon registry configuration contains a DefaultPassword value used for automatic logon. Any principal able to read the value can recover a plaintext Windows credential that may also be valid for remote access or other systems.

fix.label: Disable plaintext AutoLogon
fix.text: Disable automatic logon and remove DefaultPassword from Winlogon; use a managed kiosk or service-account design when unattended startup is required.

fix.label: Rotate the account password
fix.text: Change the affected account password and investigate whether it was reused or accessed by unauthorized local principals.

password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.title: Possible plaintext secret in a file
password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.why: A file contains a password-, secret-, API-key-, or token-like assignment with a nonempty value. The match requires validation because configuration examples can cause false positives, but a real value may grant access to applications, cloud services, databases, or infrastructure.

test.label: Confirm matching files without printing values

fix.label: Move the secret out of the file
fix.text: Store production secrets in an approved secret manager or protected operating-system credential facility and inject them only at runtime.

fix.label: Rotate confirmed secrets
fix.text: Revoke and replace any genuine credential found in plaintext, remove it from backups and version history where feasible, and restrict access to residual files.

password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.title: Possible plaintext secret on Windows
password-passwd-secret-api-key-token-s-s.why: A Windows enumeration artifact contains a password-, secret-, API-key-, or token-like assignment. Examples and placeholders can match the pattern, but a real value may expose local, domain, application, or cloud access and should be treated as compromised until validated.

test.label: Review the file access control list

fix.label: Use managed secret storage
fix.text: Move the value to Windows Credential Manager, DPAPI-protected application storage, a managed service account, or an enterprise secret manager as appropriate.

fix.label: Rotate and remove the value
fix.text: Revoke confirmed credentials, replace them with unique scoped secrets, remove plaintext copies and stale backups, and restrict the containing file's ACL.

rw-s-sid-rsa-ed25519-ecdsa-dsa-b-23e3e3c.title: SSH private key stored on disk
rw-s-sid-rsa-ed25519-ecdsa-dsa-b-23e3e3c.why: A file named like a standard SSH private key is present in the assessed user context. If the key lacks a strong passphrase or can be read by an attacker, it may provide direct access to every system that trusts its corresponding public key.

fix.label: Protect and rotate the key
fix.text: Use a strong passphrase or hardware-backed key, rotate keys whose confidentiality is uncertain, and remove the old public key from every authorized_keys file and service that trusted it.
